article_title: Quantitative Black Hole Imaging Laboratory with the Black Hole Vision App: I. Schwarzschild Spacetime
citation: Lior M. Burko. (2026). Quantitative Black Hole Imaging Laboratory with the Black Hole Vision App: I. Schwarzschild Spacetime. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21887
title: Hierarchical modular laboratory design tiering the same investigation for introductory and graduate learners
description: The investigation is structured as a tiered laboratory in which a foundational "Short Lab" covers mass triangulation and spherical symmetry constraints while an advanced "Spacetime Deep Dive" adds the lensing Jacobian, orbital instabilities, and high-rigor statistics such as inverse-variance weighting and matched-pairs t-analysis. The author states "This investigation is intentionally designed with a hierarchical modularity to accommodate a spectrum of learners," and notes simpler evaluative methods can be substituted for introductory settings so the same materials scale from foundational exploration to metrology probe.
requirements: A smartphone running the freely available Black Hole Vision app, with a calibrated meter stick mounted at a fixed distance as the measurement target
constraints: The high-rigor statistical framework "transcends the typical statistics and data analysis methods available to undergraduate students" and is intended primarily for the graduate-level Spacetime Deep Dive
target_learners: undergraduate students in introductory General Relativity courses
graduate students in General Relativity or Relativistic Astrophysics
target_learning_goals: distinguishing physical metric signatures from instrumental noise
examples: The Short Lab uses Sections 2 and 6 (mass triangulation and symmetry); the Spacetime Deep Dive uses Sections 3, 4, and 5 with GR notation and advanced statistical procedures
key_sources: Lior M. Burko. (2026). Quantitative Black Hole Imaging Laboratory with the Black Hole Vision App: I. Schwarzschild Spacetime. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21887
